findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass` body. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class is abstract. `MetricAlertFire` is a registered `GroupType` whose `detector_handler` points at this class, and `Detector.detector_handler` does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`; for any `Detector` row with `type="metric_alert_fire"` this will now raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` from inside `process_detectors`, whereas before this PR `evaluate` simply returned an empty list. Either implement the abstract members (even as stubs), keep the old concrete `DetectorHandler` subclass until the real implementation lands, or remove `detector_handler` from `MetricAlertFire`. The `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` comment is also now stale.

findings.title: Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe is built with the wrong group key
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is produced via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with group key `"group_key"`, so the handler's hook builds an occurrence whose fingerprint is `[f"{detector.id}:group_key"]` while the expected one has `[f"{detector.id}:val1"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with field-wise equality (and `DetectorEvaluationResult` compares its `result` field), so `== expected_result` cannot hold and the assertion will fail. The call should pass `"group_key"` (i.e. `expected_result.group_key`) so the fingerprints line up.

findings.title: Hook arguments `value` are never verified; several tests pass incorrect values and still pass
findings.body: `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` delegates to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event`, which ignores the `value` argument entirely. As a result nothing in the suite checks that `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` forwards the correct value (or priority) to the new hook. This is already masking mistakes in the expectations: `test_state_results_multi_group` builds the expected `group_2` occurrence with value `6` although the packet carries `10`, and `test_results_on_change`/`test_dedupe` build expectations with `6` while evaluating `100`/`8`. A regression that passed the wrong value or wrong `PriorityLevel` into the hook would go undetected. Consider having the mock embed `value`/`new_status` in `evidence_data` (or asserting on a `mock.patch.object` of the hook) so the forwarded arguments are actually checked.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still states "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Implementers reading the docstring will get the wrong contract; update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.
